players.product: Regulated electric service under the Very Large Customer (VLC) tariff, with new gas, renewable and battery generation and transmission built for Microsoft's data center campus in the I-94 corridor south of Milwaukee and the Vantage Data Centers / Oracle site at Port Washington, Wisconsin

quarterly_data.signal: WEC investor presentation (8-K Exhibit 99.1, August 2026): WEC expects to add 3.9 GW (~45%) of electric demand over 2026-2030 and forecasts weather-normalized Wisconsin segment electric sales growth of 6.0%-8.0% year-over-year in 2028-2030 (natural gas 0.7%-1.0%).
quarterly_data.figure: +3.9 GW (~45%) electric demand 2026-2030; electric sales +6.0%-8.0% a year 2028-2030

quarterly_data.signal: WEC investor presentation: the 2026-2030 capital plan invests $12.6 billion in regulated renewables (solar 3,850 MW / $7.9 billion, battery storage 2,130 MW / $2.9 billion, wind 555 MW / $1.8 billion), $6.1 billion in the thermal generation fleet (combustion turbines 3,300 MW / $5.2 billion, RICE generation 180 MW / $240 million, CCGT summer upgrades 150 MW / $280 million, coal-to-gas conversions and fuel oil backup $370 million) and $1.3 billion in 6 Bcf of LNG storage. Thermal projects include Oak Creek CTs (1,100 MW, $1,200 million estimated, in service 2027/2028), Foundry Ridge CTs (270 MW, 2028) and Red Oak Ridge CTs (1,125 MW, $1,700 million estimated, 2029/2030). Total WEC capital projection including ATC is $5,675.0 million in 2026, $7,751.5 million in 2027 and $7,851.7 million in 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: $12.6 billion renewables; $6.1 billion thermal; $1.3 billion LNG; 3,300 MW of CTs

quarterly_data.signal: WEC investor presentation: Vantage Data Centers' Port Washington campus will be part of OpenAI and Oracle's partnership for the Stargate expansion, with four data center buildings under construction on 670 acres.

WEC investor presentation: the approved Wisconsin Very Large Customer tariff applies to customers with 100 MW or more of forecasted new load, who subscribe to a portion of dedicated new generation resources; return on equity of 10.48% to 10.98% (specific ROE agreed with each customer) and a 57% equity ratio are fixed for the entire term, revenues and costs are excluded from future rate cases and earnings sharing, and on early termination the customer pays remaining net book value to the extent it cannot be repurposed.

WEC investor presentation (WEC Infrastructure offtake agreements): Sapphire Sky Wind Energy Center (250 MW) sells to Microsoft Corp under a 12-year agreement (commercial operation 2/7/23) and Hardin Solar III Energy Center (250 MW) to Microsoft Corp under a 15-year agreement (2/11/25).

WEC investor presentation: in the 2025 Wisconsin segment retail MWh deliveries mix, large C&I was 33% (residential and farm 31%, small C&I 36%), and data centers were 1% of large C&I deliveries; WEC's average asset base of $34.2 billion in 2025 is projected at $59.6 billion in 2030E (11.7% CAGR), with 15% VLC/bespoke.
quarterly_data.figure: data centers 1% of 2025 large C&I deliveries; asset base $34.2 billion (2025) to $59.6 billion (2030E)
